root_motivation: Every Claude session reads /proc/$PID/agent_session but the kernel only populates it inside CLONE_NEWAGENT. No userspace tool wraps `claude` (Claude Code) in that unshare, so downstream tools (mirror, episodic-observer, ctrace) re-derive session identity from PID-tree walks and JSONL filenames, which drop on SessionEnd-hook miss and crash recovery. agentns-claude is the thin launcher that creates the namespace at session birth so every consumer sees the same stable 128-bit id, and so PR_SET_AGENT_BUDGET_LIMITS has a namespace to apply to (runaway-session containment).
user_persona: Claude itself (headless via pevent or systemd-user units, and interactive via shell alias), plus self-review automation and any tool that needs to attribute work to a session. Run on jsy's laptop under linux-wintermute when booted; on stock kernels falls back to mock-mode for downstream dev.

acceptance_criteria.description: cargo build --release produces target/release/agentns-claude; cargo install --path . puts it in ~/.cargo/bin/; --version prints crate version.
--help is honest: lists --intent, --budget, --no-unshare, --verbose, mock-mode contract, --no-unshare fallback.
Mock mode: AGENTNS_SESSION_ID_OVERRIDE exported to child env; /tmp/agentns-mock file wins over env when both set.
Exec semantics: exits with wrapped command's exit code; non-existent command exits non-zero with a clear error.
[boot] unshare succeeds under linux-wintermute; consecutive invocations get different ids.
[boot] inheritance: grandchildren see the same agent_session id.
[boot] budget enforcement: --budget wall=2s -- sleep 60 is killed by the kernel at ~2s.
--no-unshare exits 0 on stock kernel with stderr warning; without --no-unshare exits non-zero with a clear 'kernel does not support agent namespaces' message.
README documents install, usage, mock-mode contract; CHANGELOG has v0.1.0 section.

scope: Synthesize session_id from (uid, boot_time_ns, monotonic_now_ns) under --no-unshare
Mock mode via $AGENTNS_SESSION_ID_OVERRIDE env and /tmp/agentns-mock file
exec into the wrapped command; inherit exit code
non_goals: Auto-detection of slash commands to set intent
Network namespace, cgroup, or seccomp shaping

five_whys_trace.q: Why does Claude need a launcher to wrap itself?
five_whys_trace.a: Because /proc/$PID/agent_session is empty unless something called unshare(CLONE_NEWAGENT) up the PID tree, and nothing does today.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does every downstream tool care about a stable session_id?
five_whys_trace.a: Because mirror/episodic-observer/session-index re-derive session identity from PID-tree walks and JSONL filenames; both methods drop on crash/reboot.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is a kernel-stamped id more durable than userspace identity?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the kernel populates /proc/$PID/agent_session for every descendant of the unshare even after the userspace hook process dies.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does this PRD bundle budget enforcement with namespace creation?
five_whys_trace.a: Because PR_SET_AGENT_BUDGET_LIMITS only applies inside an agent namespace; no launcher → no protection against runaway-session blowups.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is this a foundation PRD rather than part of session-postmortem?
five_whys_trace.a: Because PRDs #4 (recall-session-stamp) and #5 (session-postmortem) both depend on a session having an id from birth; this is the prerequisite.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Is --intent required or optional with a default?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Required. Optional with default silently drops attribution; PRD §6 leans required.

ambiguities_resolved.question: --budget syntax: comma vs JSON?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Comma-separated key=value pairs with --budget-file <path> escape for JSON.
